summary: As of mid-2026, the LLM landscape is dominated by OpenAI's ChatGPT/GPT family and Anthropic's Claude, which together account for the majority of both consumer web traffic and enterprise API usage, though Google Gemini has surged dramatically with ~450% year-over-year growth. The market is rapidly bifurcating between closed proprietary models (GPT, Claude, Gemini) and a maturing open-source ecosystem led by Meta Llama, DeepSeek, and Alibaba Qwen, with aggregator platforms like AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, and Google Vertex AI amplifying enterprise adoption well beyond direct-API numbers.

models.name: GPT-5 / GPT-5.1
models.popularity_notes: ChatGPT holds 53.9% of worldwide AI chatbot web-visit share in May 2026, OpenAI leads enterprise API deployments, and GPT models are available across every major aggregator including Azure OpenAI Service, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex, making its true consumption the highest of any model family.
strengths: Broadest aggregator and platform coverage
Multi-step reasoning and tool use
Largest developer ecosystem and third-party integrations
Strongest enterprise SLA and compliance support
Real-time web browsing and multimodal capabilities
models.best_for: General-purpose enterprise deployments, conversational AI, and complex multi-step reasoning at scale

models.name: Claude (Opus 5 / Fable 5.1)
models.popularity_notes: Anthropic leads enterprise API usage at 40% share (Menlo Ventures 2025), Claude holds 9.2% of worldwide chatbot web traffic in May 2026 (up 855% YoY), 75% developer adoption in Stack Overflow 2026 survey, and 49% of developers want to use Claude over the next year — the highest forward-looking intent of any model; available on AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Azure.
strengths: Highest developer forward-looking preference (49%)
Industry-leading safety and alignment
Superior long-document and complex reasoning performance
Top-ranked on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
Strong enterprise API adoption across aggregators
models.best_for: Enterprise safety-critical applications, long-context document analysis, and coding assistance

models.name: Gemini 2.x Pro / Ultra
models.popularity_notes: Gemini holds 27.9% of worldwide AI chatbot web-visit share in May 2026 (up ~450% YoY, reaching 2.9 billion monthly visits), with 27% enterprise API share, and is deeply integrated into Google Workspace, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Android — giving it unmatched distribution at the consumer and enterprise layers.
strengths: Largest context window among top-tier models
Native Google Workspace and Android integration
Strongest multimodal capabilities (video, audio, image)
Fastest year-over-year adoption growth of any major model
Available on Google Vertex AI and AWS Bedrock
models.best_for: Multimodal enterprise workflows, long-context document and video analysis, and Google ecosystem integration

models.name: Meta Llama 4
models.popularity_notes: Llama 4 is ranked the best open-source model for general reasoning in 2026 (KairnTech), has hundreds of millions of downloads on HuggingFace, is available on AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, Google Vertex AI, IBM watsonx, and Snowflake Cortex, making it the most widely deployed open-weights model in enterprise infrastructure globally.
strengths: Highest open-source model adoption across cloud aggregators
Free weights for self-hosting and fine-tuning
Strong general reasoning and coding benchmarks
Massive community ecosystem and derivative models
Available on every major cloud aggregator
models.best_for: Organizations requiring self-hosted or fine-tuned open-source models with broad cloud aggregator support

models.name: DeepSeek V4 / V4-Pro
models.popularity_notes: DeepSeek holds 4.1% of worldwide chatbot web-visit share as of May 2026 after a massive early-2025 spike, is the leading open-source model for coding benchmarks in mid-2026 (Tech-Insider), matches Claude Opus 4.x at ~80.8% on SWE-Bench Verified, and is available on AWS Bedrock and multiple aggregators at near-zero cost due to its MoE efficiency.
strengths: Industry-leading cost efficiency via mixture-of-experts architecture
Top-tier coding and reasoning benchmarks among open models
Open weights enabling self-deployment
Developed with significantly lower compute than comparable models
Strong tool use and agentic capabilities
models.best_for: Cost-sensitive coding, agentic, and reasoning workloads requiring open-weights flexibility

models.name: Qwen 3 / Qwen3-235B
models.popularity_notes: The Qwen family has been adopted by over 90,000 enterprises (Shakudo 2026), Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking leads open-weights coding benchmarks, Qwen 2.5 is cited as the top multilingual open-source model in 2026 (KairnTech), and Alibaba Cloud integration gives it strong enterprise reach across Asian and global markets.
strengths: Over 90,000 enterprise adoptions globally
Best-in-class multilingual and code capabilities
Massive parameter scale (235B) with MoE efficiency
Strong performance on real-world coding benchmarks
Available via Alibaba Cloud and multiple aggregators
models.best_for: Multilingual enterprise deployments, coding tasks, and Asian-market applications requiring open-weights models

models.name: Grok 3
models.popularity_notes: Grok holds 2.4% of worldwide AI chatbot web-visit share in May 2026 with a strong 13%+ US share, benefits from deep integration into X (formerly Twitter) giving it unique real-time social data access, and is growing rapidly through xAI API and third-party aggregator availability.
strengths: Real-time access to X/Twitter data and trending information
Strong STEM and reasoning benchmark performance
Witty and direct conversational style preferred by developers
Rapidly growing US market share
Competitive pricing for frontier-class reasoning
models.best_for: Real-time information retrieval, social media analytics, and STEM-heavy reasoning tasks

models.name: Mistral Large 3 / Magistral
models.popularity_notes: Mistral is one of Europe's largest AI companies and is cited prominently in the Stack Overflow 2026 developer survey, its models are available on AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, Google Vertex AI, and IBM watsonx giving strong aggregator reach, and the Magistral reasoning models have expanded its enterprise appeal significantly in 2026.
strengths: Strong European regulatory compliance and data sovereignty
Mixture-of-experts architecture for efficiency
Available across all major cloud aggregators
Magistral reasoning models competitive with top-tier closed models
Ministral enterprise-focused variants for cost optimization
models.best_for: European enterprises requiring GDPR compliance, multilingual support, and efficient frontier-class inference

models.name: Microsoft Phi-4
models.popularity_notes: Phi-4 is cited as a top model for high-performance reasoning in small-scale deployments (KairnTech 2026), benefits from deep Azure integration and availability on Azure AI Studio, AWS Bedrock, and Ollama for edge deployments, and Microsoft's enterprise relationships give it substantial silent adoption in on-premise and edge scenarios.
strengths: Industry-leading performance-per-parameter ratio
Ideal for edge and on-device deployment
Open weights with permissive licensing
Deep Azure and Microsoft 365 ecosystem integration
Extremely low inference cost
models.best_for: Edge deployments, on-device AI, and cost-constrained enterprise scenarios requiring strong small-model reasoning

models.name: Perplexity Sonar
models.popularity_notes: Perplexity holds 1.3% of worldwide AI chatbot web-visit share in May 2026, its API (Sonar) is heavily used by developers for real-time web-grounded search and retrieval tasks, and it has become a significant aggregator of underlying LLMs (Llama, Mistral, Claude) for search-augmented applications, with strong developer adoption via OpenRouter.
strengths: Native real-time web search grounding
Aggregates best underlying models for search tasks
Low cost for search-augmented generation
Strong developer adoption via API and OpenRouter
Cited sources reduce hallucination in retrieval tasks
models.best_for: Real-time search-augmented generation, research assistants, and applications requiring grounded, up-to-date information

models.name: Microsoft Copilot (Azure OpenAI)
models.popularity_notes: Microsoft Copilot holds 1.3% of worldwide AI chatbot web-visit share in May 2026 but represents a much larger enterprise footprint through Azure OpenAI Service — the primary channel through which Fortune 500 companies consume GPT models — making its true enterprise adoption substantially larger than web-traffic figures suggest.
strengths: Deepest Microsoft 365 and Teams integration
Enterprise compliance, data residency, and SOC2/HIPAA support
Azure OpenAI infrastructure used by majority of Fortune 500
GitHub Copilot developer tooling with 1M+ paid subscribers
Unified billing and procurement through existing Microsoft agreements
models.best_for: Enterprise Microsoft ecosystem deployments requiring compliance, Office 365 integration, and centralized procurement
